newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aussie Home cuts mortgage rate after RBA easing.
newsitem.headline: Aussie Home cuts mortgage rate after RBA easing.

text.p: Aussie Home Loans said it would reduce its standard variable mortgage rate by 50 basis points to 6.49 percent following the Reserve Bank of Australia's monetary policy easing earlier on Wednesday.
Aussie is Australia's biggest non-bank lender.

Aussie said its new standard variable rate, previously at 6.99 percent, was now at the lowest standard variable interest rate offered by any major lender in Australia in the last 30 years. The new rate comes into effect for new borrowers from July 31 and existing borrowers on September 23.

"The Reserve Bank has responded to further evidence of Australia's consistently low inflation rate and the rate drop will allow the small business sector to employ more people and expand their operations," managing director John Symond said.

"Borrowers can expect to see record low interest rates levels for the foreseeable future and, unlike some of the banks, we are keen to continue passing on full rate cuts made by the Reserve Bank," he said.
Symond said home loan borrowers were now enjoying the best conditions in the home finance market for 30 years.
Aussie has more than A$5.5 billion worth of loans written. The loans are funded by Macquarie Bank Ltd securitisation arm, PUMA.
